message.content:
**Allele frequency of rs7412 (APOE e2) in Europeans**

| Source | Population | Minor allele frequency (MAF) |
|--------|------------|------------------------------|
| **gnomAD v3.1** (European non-Finnish) | EUR | ≈ 0.05 (≈ 5 %) |
| **1000 Genomes Project** (EUR superpopulation) | EUR | ≈ 0.04–0.06 depending on sub‑group |

> **Interpretation:**  
> In most European cohorts the minor allele (the “e2” allele encoded by rs7412) occurs at roughly 4–6 % of chromosomes. This translates to about 8–12 % of individuals carrying at least one copy of the allele (assuming Hardy–Weinberg equilibrium).

> **Caveats & notes**  
> * Frequencies can differ slightly between sub‑populations (e.g., Northern vs Southern Europe).  
> * The figure above reflects the *minor* allele frequency; if you’re interested in the *major* allele (rs429358), it’s the opposite (~95 %).  
> * These numbers come from large public datasets (gnomAD and 1000 Genomes); they may not perfectly match every local cohort.

If you need more precise figures for a specific country or demographic group, let me know!
